passage:
Day 1. Kiran listened to Salma's voice note about the project and thought she sounded flat and tired. Kiran worried Salma was upset and did not reply for hours.

Day 2. On a video call, Salma's voice sounded nasal and thin, and Kiran wondered again. Kiran asked, "Are you okay? You sound low." Salma laughed. "The network is terrible and I am outside on a noisy road."

Day 4. Kiran now checks before guessing. When Salma's voice note came again, thin and fuzzy, Kiran replied, "Voice notes are so compressed. Everything okay on your end?" Salma answered with a cheerful thumbs-up.

qa.q: What did Kiran think of Salma's flat voice on day 1, and what was the truth?
qa.a: Kiran thought Salma sounded upset and tired and worried, but the flat sound was due to a poor network and noise. Voice notes lose many cues.

qa.q: What did Kiran do differently by day 4?
qa.a: Kiran checked in with a question about how things were, instead of guessing from the sound of the voice note.

qa.q: How might Salma have felt about Kiran's worry?
qa.a: Salma seems to have found it touching or funny, since Salma laughed and answered cheerfully.

grounding: Illustrates a tired-sounding voice on a call or voice note that may just be a poor connection, resolved by checking in instead of guessing.

subtype: Voice on calls and voice notes [Mismatch]
passage: Elder here, Sharmila. Mahima, you asked why I ring instead of relying on voice notes. Let me tell you. Years ago, my colleague's voice on the phone sounded flat, breathy and very tired. I decided she was sulking and I was cold to her for a week. Then I met her and she was cheerful. The line had been bad and her phone was old. Voices on the phone lose so much: the face, the small smile, everything. Now if someone sounds tired or short, I do not decide. I say, "You sound a bit low, is it the line or is something on your mind?" It costs nothing and saves me from foolish weeks.

qa.q: How long was Sharmila cold to the colleague?
qa.a: Sharmila was cold for a week.

qa.q: What was Sharmila thinking about the colleague's flat voice at first, and what was the truth?
qa.a: Sharmila decided the colleague was sulking, but the flat voice came from a bad line and an old phone. Phone voices lose the face and small smile.

qa.q: What does Sharmila say now when someone sounds low on the phone?
qa.a: Sharmila asks whether it is the line or something on the person's mind, instead of deciding.

qa.q: How might the colleague have felt when Sharmila was cold for a week?
qa.a: The colleague was probably confused or hurt without knowing why, since the cause was only a bad line.

grounding: Elder's story about a flat or breathy voice on a phone line that may be a poor connection, where checking in beats guessing.

subtype: Voice on calls and voice notes [Mismatch]
passage: Wasim had been on the offshore rig for three weeks, and the only way to talk was a crackling satellite call on Sunday nights, with a twenty-minute limit. This Sunday his voice came through flat and thin, every word slightly delayed. "Yeah. Fine. Work's fine." Rehana, in their flat in Kochi, felt her chest tighten. He sounded exhausted, or low, or angry with her. Was it about the argument before he left? She almost spent the precious minutes asking what was wrong in a hurt voice. Instead she said, "Your voice sounds really flat tonight. Is that the line, or are you okay?" A pause, a crackle. Then he laughed, and even the laugh sounded tinny. "It's the line! It makes me sound like a robot. I'm actually in a good mood; we finished the pipe job early." Rehana laughed too. "Robot husband. Good to know."

qa.q: How long were the satellite calls allowed to last?
qa.a: Twenty minutes.

qa.q: What did Rehana fear Wasim's flat voice meant?
qa.a: Rehana felt anxious and hurt, fearing he was exhausted, low or still angry about their argument.

qa.q: Why was Rehana's question a good use of the short call?
qa.a: It checked gently whether the flatness was the line or a real problem, instead of spending the minutes on a hurt guess.

qa.q: How was Wasim actually feeling?
qa.a: He was in a good mood, pleased the pipe job had finished early; the compressed line just made him sound like a robot.

grounding: Shows a flat voice on a poor satellite line being read as tiredness or anger, and checking in revealing it was the connection.

subtype: Voice on calls and voice notes [Mismatch]
passage: Farida was on the Pune metro when Abhinav's voice note came in: "Hi Farida... the client wants... the revisions... by Monday." His voice sounded breathy and faint, as if every word cost effort. Farida frowned. Abhinav had been working late all week. Was he burning out? Sick? Annoyed about the revisions? She almost forwarded it to their manager with a worried note. Then she thought: a voice note loses everything, the face, the room, even half the sound. She got off at her stop and rang him. "Hey, your voice note sounded really tired. Are you all right?" He laughed, loud and clear now. "Sorry! I recorded it walking on the bridge with the wind blowing straight into the mic. I'm fine. Actually I'm glad about Monday, it gives us the weekend." Farida smiled. "Next time, text me." "Deal."

qa.q: Where was Abhinav when he recorded the voice note?
qa.a: Walking on the bridge, with the wind blowing into the mic.

qa.q: What did Farida worry the breathy voice note meant?
qa.a: Farida felt concerned that Abhinav might be burning out, unwell or annoyed about the revisions, since he'd worked late all week.

qa.q: Why was calling better than forwarding the note to the manager?
qa.a: A voice note loses face and sound cues, so a quick call showed the real picture, wind and a good mood, without raising a false alarm.

qa.q: How did Abhinav actually feel about the Monday deadline?
qa.a: He was glad, because it left the weekend for the work.

grounding: Shows a breathy voice note read as tiredness when it was wind noise, and a quick call replacing the guess.

"...and the report's attached," Farhan said, his voice flat and muffled through the laptop speaker.
Disha paused. "Farhan, can I ask something? You sound really low today. Everything okay?"
"Low?" A crackle. "Do I?"
"Flat. Like you've had a terrible week."
"Hang on." Rustling. His voice suddenly came through clearer. "Better?"
"Much. What happened?"
"My headset was stuffed in my hoodie pocket. And I've had a cold, so I sound like I'm talking through a pillow." He laughed. "But my week's been fine. Good, even. The report finally balanced."
"Oh, thank goodness. I was about to message your manager to go easy on you."
"Please don't! He'll give me a pep talk."
"Noted. Cold, pocket, good week."
"Exactly. Now, slide three?"

qa.a: Stuffed in his hoodie pocket.

qa.q: What did Disha think Farhan's flat voice meant?
qa.a: Disha felt concerned, reading the flat, muffled voice as a sign he was low and having a terrible week.

qa.q: Why was asking better than messaging Farhan's manager?
qa.a: Asking directly revealed that the headset and a cold were behind the flat sound, so Disha avoided a worried message about a problem that didn't exist.

qa.q: How was Farhan's week really going?
qa.a: It was fine, even good, since the report finally balanced; only the headset and his cold made him sound low.

grounding: Shows a muffled, flat voice on a call being read as low mood, and a direct check-in revealing equipment and a cold.

subtype: Voice on calls and voice notes [Mismatch]
passage:
Last winter my younger sister Tanuja moved to Pune for her first job, and we mostly talked in voice notes. One Sunday her note came through flat and breathy, words dragging, with a hiss underneath: "Yeah... work's... fine. Talk later."
I listened to it four times. She sounded exhausted, maybe miserable. I started imagining a horrible boss, loneliness, crying in her PG room. I nearly called our parents.
Instead I called her. The line crackled. "Tanu, you okay? Your voice note sounded so low."
She laughed, and the laugh broke into static. "I recorded it on the bus with the window open! And I'd just woken up from a nap. I'm fine, Kishore bhaiya, promise."
Since then, when a voice sounds flat through a phone, I remind myself it may be the line, not the person. I check before I worry.

qa.q: Where did Tanuja record the voice note?
qa.a: She recorded it on the bus with the window open.

qa.q: What was Kishore feeling after listening to the note four times?
qa.a: Kishore felt worried and anxious, imagining a horrible boss and loneliness because the voice sounded flat and tired.

qa.q: What did Kishore do instead of calling their parents, and why was it better?
qa.a: He called Tanuja directly and asked gently, which let her explain the bus noise and the nap before the worry spread.

qa.q: How might Tanuja have felt if their parents had been called?
qa.a: She might have felt embarrassed or fussed over, since she was fine and the flat sound came from the bus and a nap.

grounding: A flat, breathy voice note may come from a poor connection or noise rather than mood, so checking in beats guessing.
